newsitem.title: USA: Phillips hits snag in Mahogany production.
newsitem.headline: Phillips hits snag in Mahogany production.

text.p: Phillips Petroleum Co has stopped production from the Mahogany sub-salt wells in the Gulf of Mexico because of a mechanical problem in one of two wells, company executives said on Wednesday.

The wells have been flowed at test rates but production was halted by a plug that formed last Thursday in well tubing that trapped a wire line, Jerry Fetters, manager of North American production said.
"We're not producing because of that incident," Fetters told reporters at Cambridge Energy Research Associates energy forum in Houston.
Crews expected to clear the plug, which was formed by an icy chunk of hydrates, "in a few days," he said.
Production from the Mahogany field began in late December. The company should have five wells on line and still expects an average 22,000 barrels per day production from the field this year, he said.
Phillips and Anadarko Petroleum Corp each hold 37.5 percent stakes in the field, and Amoco Corp has a 25 percent stake.
